newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary privatisation agency, bourse to cooperate.
newsitem.headline: Hungary privatisation agency, bourse to cooperate.

text.p: Hungary's state privatisation agency APV Rt and the Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE) intend to increase their cooperation to enhance the importance of the bourse, APV said in a statement.
Under the agreement, the two will cooperate to determine the companies to be privatised and listed, and APV will inform the BSE about the schedule of public offers in good time.

The BSE's chief executive officer Josef Rotyis said earlier this month he expected the Budapest equity market capitalisation to grow as a percentage of GDP to around 20 percent in a few years' time from the current ratio of around seven percent. @
The BSE's market capitalisation was 733.08 billion forints at the end of October. In 1996 the value of shares listed on the BSE grew by more than 100 percent in dollar terms.
"The increase in the bourse's capitalisation is very important to develop the domestic capital market," APV said after its board meeting today at which Rotyis also participated.
"To encourage flotations and raise market capitalisation is an essential task of the state assets manager," APV said.@
Over the past few years several companies, including pharmaceuticals firms Richter and Egis, chemicals firms TVK and Borsodchem, were listed in the BSE after their privatisation.
